correctness.rationale: For each modulation residue, Fourier inversion exactly reduces the N-vector orthonormal condition to a 3-by-3 Hadamard condition. Every three consecutive translation rows are mutually orthogonal, enforcing projective period three; the translation order must be divisible by three. When it is, the fiber-orbit permutation has order three. Depending on the orbit length modulo three, its projective triple is a permutation of three distinct eigenvectors or one of six three-point perfect cyclic sequences. Exactly six patterns and q free phase choices per fiber give 6^d q^M, and replacing q free phases by circle phases gives 6^d disjoint M-tori. A standalone exact checker exhausts 15,773,391 candidate arrays, checks 7,488 constructive examples and independently assembles 124 full synthesis Gramians. Small tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A complete sharp existence, enumeration and topological classification of a natural critically sampled finite time-frequency family. It identifies translation-step order as a genuine nonexistence obstruction and cube-root availability as a sharp alphabet condition, with exact labelled window counts across every cyclic size and nonzero step. The three-translation rule is structurally distinct from earlier two-translation parity/mod-four cases; the precise count supports reproducible window design and enumeration.
